tips.title: Scribing Panel Lines with RB Productions Tools
tips.text: For crisp panel lines, use RB Productions' scribing tools. Choose the appropriate size (0.2mm, 0.3mm, or 0.5mm) based on your model's scale. Hold the tool like a pencil, apply gentle pressure, and follow the panel line. Start from one end and push along the line, don't pull back. For best results, use a sharp tool and scribe on lightly sanded, bare plastic.

tips.title: Photo-Etch Bending with Eduard's Jigs
tips.text: Eduard's photo-etch bending jigs help create accurate angles for details like landing gear and antennae. Before bending, lightly scratch the bending point with a sharp knife. Place the jig on a flat surface, position the photo-etch part on the jig's bend, and press gently with tweezers. Bend gradually, checking the angle frequently. For tight bends, use a sharp needle to create a precise bend.

tips.title: Airbrush Needle Cleaning with Iwata Brush Washer
tips.text: Keep your Iwata airbrush needle clean for smooth paint flow. After each color change, run Iwata Airbrush Cleaner through the brush. Then, use the Iwata Brush Washer to scrub the needle. Dip the washer in cleaner, insert it into the brush body, and rotate the trigger to scrub the needle. Rinse and dry thoroughly before resuming painting.

tips.title: Masking with Tamiya Tape vs Kabuki Tape
tips.text: Choose between Tamiya tape (thinner, more delicate) and Kabuki tape (thicker, more robust) based on your masking needs. For complex, fine maskings like air intakes, use Tamiya tape. For large, flat surfaces like wing-root merges, use Kabuki tape. Always press down firmly and use a sharp blade to trim.

tips.title: Sanding Stick Progression for Smooth Surfaces
tips.text: Achieve a smooth finish with ICM's sanding sticks. Start with 240-grit for general shaping, followed by 320-grit for removing scratches, and finish with 400-grit for a fine, smooth surface. Sand parallel to panel lines, never in circles. For hard-to-reach areas, use ICM's flexible sanding sticks. Wet-sand with water for better control and easier clean-up.
